summary: Lorna Dewaraja (1929–2014) was a historian and Buddhist studies scholar. She served as Associate Professor of History at the University of Ceylon (~1960–1978) and held a post at St Anne's College.

Lorne Ladner is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche and was an adjunct faculty member in the counseling program at Argosy University (attested 2004).

Lothar Ledderose (born 1942) works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Princeton (~1967–1968) and Harvard (~1969–1970), and held posts at Heidelberg University (Professor, ~1976–2009) and the University of Cambridge (~1992–1993).

Lothar von Falkenhausen (born 1959) works in Sinology and archaeology. He held a post at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1993) and was a visiting professor at the Research Institute for Humanity and Nature in 2003.

Louis Dumont (1911–1998) worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Marcel Mauss and attended the Institut d'ethnologie and EPHE, later holding posts at Oxford (1951–1955) and the EHESS (attested 1985).

Louis Finot (1864–1935) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who studied at the École des chartes (1884–1888). He served as the first director of EFEO (~1900–1904) and held posts at the Collège de France (1920–1935).
Louis Gabaude (born 1942) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient from circa 1980 to 2007.

Louis H. Gray (1875–1955) was a linguist, Indologist, and Iranian specialist who studied at Princeton (~1892–1896) and Columbia (~1896–1900). He held posts at Princeton (~1900–1902) and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1920–1921).
Louis Havet (1849–1925) was a linguist who studied at the EPHE under Michel Bréal and Abel Bergaigne (~1868–1872). He held a post at the Collège de France from 1885 to 1925.

Louis Komjathy (born 1971) specializes in religious studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at Boston University under Paul Rouzer and served as Assistant Professor of Chinese Religions and Comparative Religious Studies at the University of San Diego (~2008).

Louis Ligeti (1902–1987) worked in Sinology, Tibetology, and Central Asian studies. He studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1921–1925) and the University of Paris (1925–1928), where he studied under Paul Pelliot.

Louis Renou (1896–1966) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Antoine Meillet (~1919–1925). He served as Director at the University of Paris (~1937–1966) and was a member of the Institut de France (~1946–1966).

Louis de La Vallée Poussin (1869–1938) specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying under Sylvain Lévi and Hendrik Kern. He was a professor at Ghent University (~1893–1929) and Free University of Brussels (attested 1933).

Louis-Mathieu Langlès (1763–1824) was an Indologist, Sinologist, and linguist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy. He was Chief Keeper of Manuscripts at the Bibliothèque nationale and administrator at INALCO (~1795–1824).
Louise Child specializes in religious studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Leeds under Linda Hogan, studied under Ringu Tulku, and held a teaching post at Leeds.

Loukram Ibempishak Devi is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Gauhati University under Sibnath Sarma (attested 1999) and also studied under S. Shyamkishore Singh and S. Lokendrajit Singh.
Luboš Bělka (born 1958) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Masaryk University (~1978–1983) and held a post there beginning circa 1990.

Luca Maria Olivieri (born 1962) specializes in archaeology and Indology. He earned a doctorate from the Free University of Berlin (attested 2010), directed IsMEO (~2011), and became an Associate Professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice (~2020).

Lucia Dolce is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She held posts at SOAS University of London as a Lecturer in Japanese Religions (attested 2003–2007) and later as an associate professor (attested 2015).
Lucia Galli is a Tibetologist. She earned her doctorate at the University of Oxford and held an academic post there.
